tier_reason: First-party README tables against Numba 0.66 and NumPy 2.x with public scripts (benchmarks/fourway.py, bench_v016.py, evolve_bench.py, microbench.py), but no CPU model ('single core in a shared CI container'; RESULTS*.md say only x86_64, 1 core, Python 3.12.3) and no llvmlite/LLVM version, so not A; no independent run, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README summary: 5-operation fused NumPy expression 3.0x vs NumPy and 3.7x vs Numba; fib(30) 1.7x vs Numba; call/dispatch about 46 ns, 3.6x less than Numba. Four-way table: plain Hana Jit about equal to Numba (fp reduction 0.78 vs 0.74 ms, poly5 1.04 vs 0.96 ms, dot 0.80 vs 0.74 ms); evolve() 0.23, 0.22 and 0.31 ms against Numba 0.74, 0.96 and 0.74 ms, but fourway.py runs evolve(allow_fastmath=True) against plain njit without fastmath. The repo's fairer files show smaller wins: benchmarks/RESULTS-FOURWAY.md has the GA tying Numba fastmath on fp reduction (0.7 vs 0.7 ms) and the fused expression at 14.4 ms vs Numba fastmath 30.7 ms (about 2.1x, derived from page data); RESULTS-EVOLVE.md (fastmath on for both where allowed) gives a 1.19x geomean over Numba across 15 kernels; RESULTS-MICRO.md (hanajit 0.5.1) gives a 1.12x geomean over Numba across 52 workloads, driven by the dispatch rows (4.31x), with control 0.96x, recursion 0.92x and pointer 0.97x.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: LLVM -O3 through llvmlite (version not stated); Numba 0.66 compared with default njit (fastmath off) in fourway.py and bench_v016.py, njit(fastmath=True) on starred rows of evolve_bench.py; NumPy 2.x
corrections.hardware: README: single core in a shared CI container; RESULTS.md and RESULTS-MICRO.md: x86_64, 1 core, Python 3.12.3; CPU model never stated
corrections.caveats: The README's evolve() wins over Numba compare fast-math code with strict Numba: benchmarks/fourway.py calls evolve(allow_fastmath=True) but times plain njit, and evolve.py then accepts candidates within a 1e-9 relative tolerance, so the README's 'guaranteeing an identical result' does not hold for that table; against njit(fastmath=True) the fp-reduction gain disappears (RESULTS-FOURWAY.md 0.7 vs 0.7 ms). Plain scalar loops tie Numba (both LLVM); the broad 52-workload geomean is 1.12x, mostly from dispatch overhead, and a cross-function call row is 0.14x of Numba. RESULTS.md and RESULTS-MICRO.md were recorded with old versions (hanajit 0.8.0 and 0.5.1; current 0.24.0). No CPU model; the README itself says absolute times are noisy. The 10-100x over CPython claim is not a named-incumbent comparison. Numba is not in the jits baseline list (PyPy, LuaJIT, V8, HotSpot). 2 stars, alpha status.

notes: README numbers are on the page, but the four-way table pits evolve(allow_fastmath=True) against non-fastmath Numba; the repo's own fastmath-for-both files show the GA tying Numba on fp reduction and a 1.19x (15 kernels) or 1.12x (52 workloads, dispatch-driven) geomean. Tier stays C; claim corrected, so recorded as downgrade of the claim, not the tier. Shortcomings: fastmath-vs-strict comparison, no CPU model, stale results files, baseline off-list, 2 stars.

tier_reason: The README Performance table compares one Collatz kernel against PyPy 3.11.15 (52.8 ms vs ppy run 41.7 ms) with tool versions and C flags, but names no CPU for that table and ships no PyPy, Cython, mypyc or Nuitka script; the reproducible suite (examples/15_algorithms, CPU named) covers C, Numba, Mojo and Codon, not PyPy. First-party, partial methodology: C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Collatz longest chain below 300000, kernel wall time, ten fresh processes: ppy run (Python integer semantics, overflow guards) 41.7 +/- 1.8 ms vs PyPy 3.11 52.8 +/- 0.5 ms (about 1.27x, derived from page data) and CPython 3.14 1068.8 +/- 5.5 ms; ppy build --unsafe 30.8 ms vs Numba 32.5 ms, clang -O3 32.8 ms, gcc -O3 41.9 ms, Codon 42.1 ms. ppy run excludes a one-time ~640 ms build. In the eight-kernel suite (examples/15_algorithms) Numba leads on six of the eight kernels by 10-30%.
corrections.hardware: Not stated for the README Collatz table ('one machine'); examples/15_algorithms/measurements.json for the same 0.6.0 release records Intel Core Ultra 9 386H, 16 cores, WSL2 (probably the same machine, unconfirmed)
corrections.caveats: Single kernel against PyPy; the README table names no CPU and the repository has no script for the PyPy, Cython, mypyc or Nuitka rows, so those rows are not reproducible from the repo. The eight-kernel suite (examples/15_algorithms, code in compare/, Intel Core Ultra 9 386H, gcc 13.3 / clang 22.1 -O3) compares against C, Numba, Mojo and Codon, not PyPy, and there Numba leads six of eight kernels by 10-30%. PPy compiles an annotated, statically analyzable subset of Python while PyPy runs arbitrary Python. ppy run times exclude the ~640 ms first-run build. Pre-1.0 (0.6.0; minor releases may change the language), 15 stars.

notes: Numbers match the README exactly; 1.27x over PyPy is one kernel with no PyPy script and no CPU named for that table, so C stands. Shortcomings: single-kernel PyPy comparison, PyPy row not reproducible from repo, Numba faster on 6 of 8 kernels in the project's own suite, pre-1.0.

tier_reason: README speedup table versus the regex crate and PCRE2 JIT comes from public criterion code (benches/competitors.rs, same captures work per engine), but results are not committed (benches/results is gitignored) and no CPU model or rustc version is stated, so not A; first-party, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Speedup vs the regex crate (README table): regexr-jit 3.91-4.09x on log_parsing (pcre2-jit 3.57-3.71x), 1.95-1.99x on url_extraction (pcre2-jit 2.10-2.13x), 1.43-1.44x on unicode_letters (pcre2-jit 1.65-1.72x), 1.33-1.43x on html_tags (pcre2-jit 0.80-0.85x), 1.15-1.19x on word_boundary (pcre2-jit 0.72-0.74x), 1.00-1.11x on email_validation, 0.88-1.01x on alternation. Non-JIT regexr is 0.80-0.87x of regex on log_parsing, url_extraction and html_tags.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: cargo bench with criterion 0.8 (benches/competitors.rs, --features full for JIT); default bench profile, rustc version not stated; regex 1.13, fancy-regex 0.19, pcre2 crate 0.2
corrections.caveats: Benchmark code is public (benches/competitors.rs, run_benchmarks.sh prints CPU and rustc but the results are gitignored), yet the README states no hardware or toolchain and the table is undated. The JIT loses to PCRE2 JIT on url_extraction and unicode_letters and ties regex on email_validation and alternation; the non-JIT engine is slower than regex on several patterns, and the README itself recommends the regex crate for 99% of uses. Better filed under regex-engines (wave 3), whose baselines are PCRE2 and Rust regex; it is a regex JIT, not a language JIT, and none of the jits baselines (PyPy, LuaJIT, V8, HotSpot) apply.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 27 stars, 1 fork; crates.io regexr 0.6.0, about 36k downloads (20.8k recent)

notes: Numbers match the README; fair same-work criterion harness but no hardware/toolchain and no committed results, so C. Suggest category override to regex-engines (there Rust regex and PCRE2 are listed baselines, making baseline_in_list true). Not a duplicate of any listed project. Shortcomings: loses to PCRE2 JIT on 2 of 7 rows, non-JIT slower than regex, no hardware stated.
